CENP-B box screen across the DToL satellite repertoire

Generated 2026-08-13 · module 06_cenpb_box

Terminology. A CENP-B box is a functional motif that binds the CENP-B protein. Here we detect sequence matches only, so we call them motifs / candidate boxes; none is a confirmed functional box (protein binding not tested).

Bottom line. The canonical CENP-B motif ([CT]TTCGTTGGAA[AG]CGGGA) as an exact match is confined to human α-satellite — 0 exact canonical motifs in any of the 162 DToL species with satellites. A ±5-flank test flags box-like motifs in 20 species, strongest in birds: the goshawk consensus CTTTTTTGGAAACGGGA is 15/17 identical to the canonical box, differing only at the CpG (positions 4–5, CpG→TT). These are strong candidate divergent boxes — near-canonical but lacking the CENP-B-essential CpG (the exact broad motif, which fixes that CpG, therefore scores 0). Their functionality is untested (no protein-binding assay).

What was searched

inputall.satellites.txt — every candidate satellite-repeat array called across the DToL assemblies (candidates, not curated satellites). Restricted to the 325 published species (tree tips); 12 out-of-set species excluded. "Uncapped" = every candidate array of each species, both strands (~20.3 million arrays across the 162 of 325 species that carry satellite annotations) — not a ≤500-monomer subsample.

Human HG002 benchmarks

Both methods were validated on human satellites: α-satellite (positive; carries the box) and HSat 1/2/3 (negative; lacks it).

Canonical boxes are ~50,000× denser per Mbp in α-satellite than HSat; both methods separate the controls cleanly.

Method 1 — exact IUPAC motif parsing (Fachinetti)

Three exact IUPAC tiers (canonical / broad / degenerate; Barra & Fachinetti, bioRxiv 2026.05.25.727640), both strands, scored as enrichment over a dinucleotide-preserving null (first-order Markov ≈ Altschul–Erikson doublet shuffle; validated against an explicit shuffle on the α-sat benchmark, 4,283× vs 4,524×).

The two quantities are shown first as bar charts, then combined in a scatter.

(i) Enrichment over the dinucleotide null (obs/exp), per clade × tier (broken y-axis; α-satellite ≫ DToL). Canonical = 0 in all DToL clades; HSat canonical = 5 boundary hits (hatched).
(ii) Motif density — exact IUPAC hits per Mbp, per clade × tier (broken y-axis).
(iii) Scatter of enrichment (i) vs density (ii). A real box needs both: only α-satellite sits top-right. HSat canonical is a lone point at ~0.03/Mbp (5 boundary hits → high enrichment but ~0 density — not a box). DToL clades sit near the null (enrichment ≈ 1).
clade n_species canonical broad degenerate
Vertebrates 23 0.0 1.39 0.51
Invertebrates 91 0.0 0.96 0.25
Plants 48 0.0 1.15 3.01

Note. This uses composition-corrected enrichment, not raw hits/Mbp — raw density inflates plants (AT-rich, more satellite bp); under the dinucleotide null vertebrates actually edge plants on the broad tier.

Method 2 — songbird ±5-flank test (Formenti et al., Cell 2026)

For each species we collect its box windows (17-mers within ≤5 substitutions of canonical, both strands) together with their ±5 flanking bp (27-bp windows), and build a position frequency matrix. Per position we compute the information content in bits, IC = 2 + Σb pb log₂ pb (0 = random, 2 = fully conserved). Then:

  • y-axis — box information = mean IC over the 17 box positions (how conserved the motif itself is);
  • x-axis — flank information = mean IC over the 10 flanking positions (±5), a built-in negative control.

A real motif is conserved at the box but random in the flanks → high y, low x → above the box=flank diagonal (Δ = box − flank > 0).

Box vs flank information, coloured by identity to the canonical CENP-B motif. A candidate box = high identity and above the box=flank diagonal (box-specific). α-satellite (red star) = the functional box; HSat (grey ×) = negative. Birds (goshawk, takahē, ptarmigan) are the most box-specific vertebrates; falcons sit on the diagonal (conserved satellite, not a candidate box).

Is the box-like identity real? (shuffle-the-motif null)

A short 17-bp motif matches partly by base composition alone, so we calibrated identity by shuffling the motif (same composition, order destroyed).

A motif of this composition matches canonical only ≈30% by chance (left), whereas observed consensus identities are 70–94% (right; median +44 above chance, birds +58 to +63). So the box-like matches are real arrangement similarity, not a short-motif composition artifact (`cenpb_identity_shuffle_null.py`).

Why the two methods disagree on birds

The goshawk motif is 15/17 identical to canonical; its only two substitutions land on the 5′ CpG (positions 4–5) that all three IUPAC tiers hold fixed (the TTCG anchor). So position-based IUPAC matching scores 0, while the distance-based songbird ≤5-substitution search (no fixed position) finds 1,722 windows. The eroded position is a CpG — a CENP-B contact base and a methylation/deamination hotspot — which is exactly why it is a candidate divergent box, not a canonical one.
